title: Factory
about: A body of work's repositories, workflows and hires.

terms.meaning: a named grouping in the store: the repositories a body of work is on, the workflows it offers, and the agents it hires into their steps.

a folder of the person's machine a factory mounts for every local step of its runs, beside its repositories, marked read-only (`:ro`) or writable (`:rw`) as docker compose marks one; kept in the factory's own file, never in its template. A writable one is writable only where a step's fence writes, and is not the run's workspace: nothing commits or lands what a step writes there.

the settings of a harness a factory gives every session of its runs' steps on it, on top of the repository's own: for Claude Code, through the Agent SDK's settings option, never a file written into the repository. A factory sets `attribution`, `includeGitInstructions` and `language` alone, each changing what a session writes or says and none what it may reach or run; kept in the factory's own file, never in its template, and frozen on a run at its start.

the one way a factory is read and written — its file, and the level, rules and servers the store keeps beside it: `FactoryDoor` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/factories/factories.store.ts`, its files layer at the store's root a program is given and a memory one, each refusing a write that breaks the model's `Factory`.

a person's change of what a factory offers, hires and schedules — attach, detach, hire, fire, schedule, unschedule — judged by `wiringRefusal` and applied by `rewired` (`packages/agent-orchestrator/src/wiring/wiring.ts`), whose contract proves that a change which would hire or schedule outside the factory's offer is refused; the door's decode through the model `Factory` refuses a factory written that does.

which condition the controller says of a factory made from a template: `Applied`, whether its base holds the template, or `ConflictsPending`, whether an upgrade waits on a person's choice. Its status is `True` or `False`, and the sentence a person reads is its `message`; written by `condition` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/applied/applied.verb.ts`.

why a factory's condition holds or not, one word: `Rendered`, `Upgraded`, `TemplateInvalid`, `VersionDrift`, `ParamsChanged`, `ContentChanged`, `VersionUnknown` or `UpgradePending` for `Applied`; `NoUpgrade`, `Merged` or `Conflicts` for `ConflictsPending`. A status file holding another word reads as none, and the next pass writes it again; the sentence is its `message`.
a factory's name: its file's in the store, without its extension, a lowercase slug of at most 40 characters.
what Nemia is to know about a factory, `NEMIA.md` by default; no step is told it.
the rules and policies of one factory, a file kept in your store with it, `~/.agent-workflows/factories/<name>/RULES.md`, told to every agent hired into it.

whether a factory's runs follow merged revisions, `follow`, each new filing taking the workflow, agents, skills and rules the files hold then, or stay `pinned`, the default, keeping what they resolved until `nemia refresh`.
a factory's choice of the agent that does one step of a workflow.

a factory made portable: a folder whose manifest, nemia.yaml, declares its version, parameters and hires, beside its workflows, agents and skills, or an archive of one `nemia template pack` wrote; keyed by its source, as `Template` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/templates/templates.model.ts`.
where a template is read from: its folder or its archive, by its whole path, checked when a template is written and read by name alone, so a factory's file written before the check still reads.

the one way a template's folder or archive is read, written and packed: `TemplateDoor` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/templates/templates.store.ts`, rooted as the Factory door is, its files layer and a memory one, each refusing a tree whose name or paths `TemplateTreeWrite` refuses. The template's lint is the verbs', not the door's.

the template a factory was made from by `nemia factory apply`, or taken over by `nemia factory adopt`, as its file records it under `template`: the template's source (a folder or archive by its whole path, or the name of a builtin template, resolved on every read), the version the factory wants, and the parameters given with `--set`.

a factory made by hand taken over in place by a template: `nemia factory diff <name> --template …` previews it as a plan with its digest, and `nemia factory adopt … --plan <digest>` writes it, the render staged as the factory's base and tree and the template named in its file; its name, repositories, schedules, instruction, cards, runs and stats stay. The plan is `AdoptPlan`, judged by `adoptRefusal` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/adopt/adopt.ts`.

a template that comes with Nemia: a folder holding its nemia.yaml in the templates workspace (`packages/templates/<name>`), found by path from the orchestrator's own folder (`BUILTIN_TEMPLATES` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/templates/templates.store.ts`) and never imported; named by its folder's name alone at `--template` and on a factory's file, where `templatePlace` resolves it on every read.

`${{ parameters.<name> }}`, written in a template's text: a render writes it with the parameter's value in every string of a document and in every text it writes — a step's and an agent's instructions, NEMIA.md, RULES.md (`substitute` and `interpolated` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/applied/params.ts`) — and copies a carried file (a script, a skill's files, a schema) byte for byte; `nemia template lint` refuses a name nemia.yaml does not declare (`packages/agent-orchestrator/src/template/check.ts`). A shell's `$VAR` and `${VAR}` are none.
